study_identification.author_journal_year: Coupé et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2022
study_identification.title: Hippocampal-amygdalo-ventricular atrophy score: Alzheimer disease detection using normative and pathological lifespan models

study_characteristics.study_objective: To develop and validate a new MRI-based score (HAVAs) for Alzheimer's disease (AD) detection and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) prognosis using lifespan trajectories of brain structures.

dataset_name.answer: C-MIND, NDAR, ABIDE, ICBM, IXI, OASIS, ADNI

quality_checking_detail.answer: For all the training subjects detected as failure by the automatic QC RegQCNet (Denis de Senneville et al., 2020), a visual assessment was performed by individually checking the input images and the segmentations produced by AssemblyNet using a 3D viewer. If the failure was confirmed by our expert, the subject was removed from training dataset.

response_variable.answer: Brain volumes: hippocampus; amygdala; inferior lateral ventrice and HAVAs

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study does not explicitly model nuisance structures like site effects. It relies on a large-scale multi-site dataset and validates on external datasets to demonstrate robustness.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: To validate our model, we built a testing dataset based on two open access databases (AIBL and MIRIAD) to perform AD versus CN diagnosis task. Therefore, we validated the generalization capacity of our method and its robustness to domain shift.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The model's performance was evaluated on a subset of the training data (ADNI).
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: Using these 33 selected areas, we performed a screening to detect the most discriminant ones in terms of classification accuracy on the training ADNI dataset in order not to use testing data during method development.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study does not use an independent dataset from the same domain for validation.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The model was validated on three external datasets (AIBL, MIRIAD, and a different split of ADNI).
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: To validate our model, we built a testing dataset based on two open access databases (AIBL and MIRIAD) to perform AD versus CN diagnosis task... In addition, we used subjects with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) from ADNI to estimate the capability of our models on prognosis task.

deviation_metric.answer: Z-score and distance from lifespan curves; HAVAs composite

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: The proposed HAVAs (i.e., the S AD score) reflects the probability for the subject under study to be a patient with AD (or a pMCI subject). The classification performance of the proposed method was validated using several metrics: balanced accuracy (BACC), specificity (SPE), sensibility (SEN) and area under the curve (AUC) based on HAVAs.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The proposed HAVAs score, based on hippocampal, amygdalo, and ventricular volumes, provides accurate AD detection and MCI prognosis, outperforming single-structure models and other state-of-the-art methods.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The study developed a novel score, HAVAs, by combining volumes of the hippocampus, amygdala, and inferior lateral ventricle. This score showed high accuracy in distinguishing AD patients from controls (AUC >= 94%) and discriminating progressive from stable MCI (AUC = 78%) on external datasets. HAVAs outperformed single-structure models, classical machine learning, and deep learning methods. The simplicity and interpretability of HAVAs make it suitable for clinical use.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The authors did not explicitly state limitations, but they mentioned that the combination of normative modeling with learned features will be investigated in future works, suggesting a potential area for improvement.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: A software package including AssemblyNet pipeline and HAVAs estimation will be made freely available as a downloadable Docker and on the volBrain platform.

general_notes.general_notes: The study provides a comprehensive evaluation of the proposed HAVAs score, including comparisons with multiple methods and sensitivity analyses. The public availability of the tools is a significant contribution.
